title: Breadcrumb
desc: A search engine for your own memory. Save anything in one tap, find it later by describing it.
about: 1st place at Hackinverse 1.0.
We save things everywhere and find them nowhere: screenshots, links, PDFs and recommendations scatter across a dozen apps, and later you remember what you saved but not where you put it.
Saving takes one tap from the share sheet, a Quick Settings tile or your voice, with no folders, tags or titles to fill in.
Finding is a single search bar. Type what you remember, like "that internship screenshot from April", and it finds the thing even when those words appear nowhere in it.
EmbeddingGemma 2 runs on the phone and scores meaning alongside keyword search, so nothing you save or type ever leaves the device. No server, no account, and search works in airplane mode.

title: NextWeeb
desc: Your personalized anime discovery and tracking web app.
about: Log in with MyAnimeList and NextWeeb copies your list, then works out what you should watch next.
Every recommendation says why it was picked: recommended by fans of a show you loved, made by a studio you like, or matching your taste in genres.
An AI chat that knows your list. Ask for something short and wholesome and it only suggests real shows you haven't seen, as clickable cards.
Your Plan to Watch ranked by how well each show fits your taste, plus stats on your top genres, studios, ratings and total watch time.
MyAnimeList login over OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, then the backend's own rotating JWTs, with no cross-site cookies.

title: Cosmic Game Sanctuary
desc: An indie game store where every sale pays the whole team.
about: Built for ETHOnline 2026, now live on Arc mainnet: Circle's chain, where USDC is the gas, so buying a game never needs a second token.
Browse without logging in, sign in with just an email, and a game you buy boots in the same tab seconds later, its build pinned to IPFS and unpacked live in the browser.
Try before you buy: play by the minute, metered from your own wallet over x402, and every cent spent trying comes off the price.

Developers drop a zip, watch it run before publishing, and split revenue with a team by email. A teammate who has never touched a wallet still gets paid the moment they accept, and the split locks at publish.
Give the agent a want and a price ceiling and it buys at the last responsible moment before a sale ends.
Buyers sign their own purchases, so the server never holds anyone's key, and uploaded games run on a separate origin so a stranger's build can never read your session.

title: Skrim
desc: A browser agent that does the task without your personal data ever leaving your machine.
about: Built for HackSpire.
AI browser agents send your screen to someone else's server, so your inbox, your bank balance and your face end up on a stranger's GPU. Skrim keeps all of that on your device.

A local pipeline reads the page, runs OCR on canvases and images, and finds private data with regexes, form-field hints and an on-device GLiNER model, swapping every value for a placeholder like <PII:EMAIL:1> before anything is sent.
The planning model only ever sees the scrubbed page, and the extension puts the real value back only at the moment it types it.
Guardrails run on the device, so no prompt can switch them off: ID and card numbers are always checked with you first, and unasked purchases or deletions are refused.
99% detection recall across 37 test pages, in Chrome, in Firefox, and in Firefox on Android.

title: Supernote
desc: Turns raw startup ideas into structured and validated projects using AI and interactive graphs.
about: Turns a rough startup idea into a structured, multi-stage plan covering market research, monetisation, scalability and technical complexity.
The plan grows on an interactive graph, with AI-suggested nodes you can edit in real time.
LangChain orchestration with vector embeddings and structured prompt pipelines keeps each suggestion aware of the rest of the plan.

title: Synapse
desc: A focused learning app using flashcards and proven memory techniques for busy students.
about: 1st place overall at the TechTrix software development hackathon 2025, iterating live on judge feedback during the finals.
A learning app for busy students, built around spaced repetition and active recall.
Customisable flashcard decks, progress tracking, and a review schedule that adapts to how well you know each card.

title: Calcutta Collective
desc: A location-first PWA that turns city discovery into small, real-world hangouts.
about: Cities are full of people, yet urban loneliness keeps rising: everyone saves cafés they never visit. The problem isn't information, it's activation.
Discovery is map-driven rather than list-driven.
Hangouts cap at 5 to 8 people so they feel intimate, and hosts approve join requests so a group chat can break the ice before anyone shows up.
Reflections after each hangout feed back into the discovery loop.
Built solo as a competition product, pitched at BPlan @ Kshitij 2025 (IIT Kharagpur) and the Hult Prize 2025 campus round.

title: ResQNet
desc: A unified platform for rapid, coordinated emergency response.
about: Best Beginner Team at HackForge, for a 12-hour build spanning two mobile apps and a web platform.
One platform connecting first responders, emergency services and civilians.
Real-time updates, live location tracking and instant communication, for when every second counts.

title: AURA
desc: An AI-powered healthcare assistant with medical image analysis, smart health records, and nearby hospital/doctor discovery.
about: Built at StatusCode2.
A digital vault for your health records.
ML models analyse uploaded scans for fractures and brain tumours, and a photo is enough to identify a medication.
Finds nearby hospitals and doctors in real time.
An AI chatbot explains medical information in plain language.

title: EchoWall
desc: Aggregates content from all your social media platforms into one unified, interactive feed.
about: Pulls posts, photos and updates from all your social platforms into one customisable feed.
Stay connected without the constant app-switching.
